bull.t: High product-level gross margin and revenue growth
bull.b: Sustained ~76% gross margins and double-digit TTM revenue growth point to attractive unit economics for neffy. Durable product-level profitability supports scalability as volumes rise, enabling the company to absorb marketing and field investments and improve operating leverage over time.

bull.t: Rapid commercial traction and growing installed base
bull.b: A large and expanding installed base, strong YoY prescription growth and an enlarged field force create a durable commercial foundation. Repeat prescribers and school program adoption increase refill predictability, strengthening recurring revenue potential and long-term market penetration.

bull.t: Regulatory and international approvals broaden addressable market
bull.b: Label expansion and approvals in Canada and the EU materially expand the eligible population and enable partner-led launches. These structural regulatory wins increase long-term market opportunity, allow geographic diversification, and support partner commercialization without proportionate US SG&A buildup.

bear.t: Substantial negative operating cash flow and cash burn
bear.b: Large, persistent negative operating cash flow signals ongoing funding needs and elevates financing risk. Even with recent cash on hand, continued high burn could force equity raises, dilute shareholders or constrain investment choices, making long-term planning and execution contingent on capital access.

High and growing SG&A reflects necessary customer acquisition spend but creates a heavy fixed-cost base. If refill conversion or payer wins lag, the company may struggle to generate sufficient operating leverage, prolonging losses and raising the bar for profitable scale.

bear.t: Access barriers and material prescription abandonment
bear.b: Prior authorization requirements, high abandonment and a ~50% gross-to-net drag structurally reduce realized revenue and slow conversion of prescriptions to fills. These persistent access frictions increase revenue variability and require durable payer solutions to sustain long-term growth.
